verify.note: Each hook against the original from one state: every register with R and all game memory after every JP of the figure routine (when it has returned) and at every CALL before which the sprites change (when the routine starts); after the loop's play the sprites against a model of the routine for every figure drawn since the last play, and the model against the pixels the original has just copied to the screen; no sprite on after a fade or a scene; on Enhanced against the painted map.

status.title: Olli and Lissa II: Halloween
status.build: olli_and_lissa_2_sprites.nex dedec792 (nothing of the game changes: every moving figure a sprite on its own pixels, white, Olli with a black edge; the original's pace) + enhanced 2744a1af (the 70 figures painted, a first pass)
status.software: Verify IDENTICAL on the rzxarchive's whole recording (116,586 frames), both builds: 193,740 draws, 82,619 plays, 193,737 figures (every register with R and all game memory after each hook; after a play the sprites against a model of the routine and the model against the pixels the original has just copied to the screen; no sprite on after 339 fades and scenes; on Enhanced against the painted map); unit PASS (35 cases); 10 of 10 broken builds detected; ROM path check pass; the hooks within 0.004% of the original's time over the recording, at most 0.4 frames lost or gained in any 10 seconds
status.hardware: untested (the patch runs from its menu in OverSpec, Enhanced on)
status.next: the owner's review of the painting; hardware test

techniques.target: the game's figure routine, its copy to the screen and the screen unchanged; each figure's sprites lie on the pixels the copy then shows
a figure's graphic address and size give its painted tiles (an index in the state page, the tiles in pages at slot 2), sent whole to the pattern port
two pattern sets: a pass's pictures go into the set no sprite shows; the play's hook switches the attributes to it and the sets change over
HLIB_R_IN / hlib_r_set / HLIB_R_OUT in the figure routine's hook and in the hook before the play, the fade and the scene (the game keeps a flag in R and reads R)
one window a figure: the hook's work and the game's routine at 28 MHz, the routine's own time by kind, shift and class of y waited out; the play's hook is owed and given back in the figures' windows
Sinclair's ROM as the alt image with the hooks from 0x2800; the game runs no ROM code

pacing.coverage: The rzxarchive's whole recording (116,586 frames); the figure routine's own time for every kind, shift and y from runs of the routine itself at build time; hook time on the simulator's line clock. No JNext or hardware timing.
pacing.result: Nothing syncs the game to the frame: a draw's hook and the routine run at 28 MHz and the routine's own time is waited out; the play's hook is owed and given back in the draws' windows. Over the whole recording the hooks take 0.004% less (white) and 0.002% less (painted) than the original's draws and plays; in any 10 seconds the game loses at most 15,629 T on the original (0.2 frames) and gains at most 29,572 T.

dependencies.coverage: Every screen writer of the first 20,000 frames (survey); the figure routine, its five JPs, the copy to the screen, the fade and the scene read and modelled; every CALL or JP of those four routines in the game's code found by the build; the whole recording replayed through the hooks.
dependencies.result: Nothing of the game's memory or screen changes. The game runs no ROM code. Interrupts are never on in the recording. The game keeps a flag in R and reads R: every hook leaves R as the original.

feasibility.decision: Sprites laid over the figures the game still draws, as the first and the third game (owner 2026-11-20 for those: 'White plus painted (Recommended)'): white with a black edge where the game has a mask, and an Enhanced set painted in a first pass.
feasibility.next_experiment: Hardware: the checklist in games/olli_and_lissa_2.md; the game's speed against the original over a minute of play: within 2%.
